subject.title: Dashboard: widget write-back — a setState bridge capability + persisted widget state

question: Should dashboard widget write-back proceed as a bundled OpenClaw capability, and must its state storage use plugin KV/shared SQLite rather than per-widget JSON files?
rationale: The request changes iframe-to-parent trust, persistent runtime state, Gateway RPC surface, and dashboard product scope, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent storage/security direction.

options.title: Sponsor With SQLite/Plugin-KV Storage
options.body: Proceed with the feature only after the dashboard base lands and the implementation uses an approved SQLite/plugin-state owner plus bridge/security regression proof.

options.title: Approve A Named JSON-State Exception
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept the per-widget JSON store and document why this state is a named product artifact outside the normal SQLite policy.

options.title: Defer Or Reject Bundled Write-Back
options.body: Leave stateful custom widgets outside bundled OpenClaw until the dashboard stack, plugin API, or ClawHub distribution story is clearer.

recommendation.title: Sponsor With SQLite/Plugin-KV Storage
recommendation.body: Proceed with the feature only after the dashboard base lands and the implementation uses an approved SQLite/plugin-state owner plus bridge/security regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is the Control UI plugin-tab seam and adjacent plugin storage precedent this feature would extend.
